candidates.explanation: The framework-neutral operation, provider port, cancellation, idle timeout, commit-aware SSE failure handling, and provider redaction are clear. However, assistant behavior is scattered across generic top-level layers rather than colocated under one capability root. Its shared generic boundary/result wrapper spans stream and job handling, weakening native channel contracts and violating the universal-wrapper prohibition.

The capability is coherently colocated apart from justified runtime entrypoints. It defines a framework-neutral use case and capability-owned provider port, uses a dedicated SSE Route Handler with abort propagation and per-read idle timeout, handles failures differently before and after commitment, preserves channel-native HTTP/SSE/job outcomes, and contains provider details in infrastructure.

The proposal correctly uses a framework-neutral generation use case, provider seam, dedicated SSE route, abort propagation, idle timeout, post-commit error events, and provider-safe contracts. Its files are scattered across generic application/domain/infrastructure roots, and it explicitly shares a generic result/event wrapper across HTTP, stream, and job. Although adapters perform separate mappings, that universal wrapper violates the rubric.

The design colocates assistant behavior under a capability root with justified Route Handler and worker surfaces. It provides a framework-neutral application boundary and capability-shaped provider port, correctly specifies cancellation, idle-only timeout, and commit-sensitive SSE failures, preserves native HTTP/stream/job contracts while sharing semantic primitives, and confines provider data and errors to the adapter.
